nodes.subject: AirPods over two years discussion
nodes.object: The thread contains materially different model, workload, exposure, service, and outcome reports: annoyance near two years under very heavy use, repeated six-to-eight-month replacement under motorcycle work exposure, and continued use at three years with reduced runtime.

support_spans.exact_quote: At about the two year mark mine start to have battery or sound issues. They are still usable so I give them to family but I am a heavy user (often 16+ hours a day) so for me they become annoying.

I’m based in the UK I got the pair I bought replaced in 2019 under the repair programme and since then I’ve had them replaced every 6-8 months under consumer law I ride a motorcycle for my job, my AirPods are in my ears while I’m riding
Just hit the 3-year mark on my 2nd gen AirPods and they're doing fine!
The only downside to them being older is that the battery life isn't quite as good as when they were new but they've never died on me before

accepted_phrases: The captured AirPods thread contains heterogeneous, scoped experiences from heavy, occupational, and three-year users; it supports variability and missing controls, not a universal deadline or a ranking of the four frozen listings.

nodes.subject: battery state-of-health overview
nodes.object: State of health compares a battery with ideal or specified condition, generally decreases with time and use, and lacks one universally agreed determination method.

support_spans.exact_quote: State of health ( SoH ) is a figure of merit of the condition of a battery (or a cell , or a battery pack ), compared to its ideal conditions.
Typically, a battery's SoH will be 100% at the time of manufacture and will decrease over time and use.
As SoH does not correspond to a particular physical quality, there is no consensus in the industry on how SoH should be determined.

accepted_phrases: Battery state of health is a condition metric relative to ideal or specified condition, normally decreases with time and use, and has no single industry determination method; it does not supply an exact TWS model decay rate or deadline.

nodes.subject: battery memory-effect overview
nodes.object: True memory effect is described for nickel-cadmium rechargeable batteries; lithium-based cells are not normally subject to it, although rechargeable batteries still have finite lifetimes and lose storage capacity with age.

support_spans.exact_quote: Memory effect , also known as battery effect , lazy battery effect , or battery memory , is an effect observed in nickel-cadmium rechargeable batteries that causes them to hold less charge.
In particular, lithium-based cells, not normally subject to the memory effect, may change their voltage levels so that a virtual decrease of capacity may be perceived by the battery control system.
All rechargeable batteries have a finite lifespan and will slowly lose storage capacity as they age due to secondary chemical reactions within the battery whether it is used or not.

accepted_phrases: True memory effect is defined for nickel-cadmium rechargeable cells, while lithium-based cells are not normally subject to it; rechargeable batteries still age, but the overview does not rank the four listings or set a universal failure deadline.

nodes.subject: device-pairing overview
nodes.object: Pairing or bonding creates an initial linkage between devices so they can communicate, with a Bluetooth headset and mobile phone as a common example.

support_spans.exact_quote: Pairing , sometimes known as bonding , is a process used in computer networking that helps set up an initial linkage between computing devices to allow communications between them.
The most common example is used in Bluetooth , [ 1 ] where the pairing process is used to link devices like a Bluetooth headset with a mobile phone .

accepted_phrases: Pairing is the initial linkage that permits devices such as a Bluetooth headset and mobile phone to communicate; this generic definition does not diagnose the root cause of one silent earbud.

nodes.subject: stereophonic-sound overview
nodes.object: Stereo reproduction commonly uses two independent audio channels, which explains why left and right channel symptoms can differ but does not identify a hardware, charging, battery, or pairing cause.

support_spans.exact_quote: Stereophonic sound , commonly shortened to stereo , is a method of sound reproduction that recreates a multi-directional, 3-dimensional audible perspective.
This is usually achieved by using two independent audio channels through a configuration of two loudspeakers (or stereo headphones )

accepted_phrases: Stereo commonly uses two independent audio channels; that architecture permits asymmetric symptoms but does not diagnose battery, charging, pairing, cable, driver, or software causes.

nodes.subject: complete TWS listing matrix
nodes.object: Audit all four complete frozen seller bodies without treating their wording as independent durability testing. The FOYCOY X10 page displays SKU B09P3Q59J9, $29.99, a 93 percent rating over 12 reviews, up to 6 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, one lithium-ion battery, and seller troubleshooting text that mentions charging-contact oxidation, earbud-to-earbud pairing, and reset. The renewed Plantronics BackBeat FIT 3100 page displays SKU B07NX25KXB, $59.95, a 60 percent rating over 81 reviews, up to 5 hours plus 10 case hours, model 211855-99-cr, one lithium-polymer battery, and app firmware-update wording. The renewed Soundcore Liberty page displays SKU B07WQSD5QM, $30.99, no reviews, 8 hours per charge and 100 hours with the case, model A3912, and one lithium-polymer battery. The TOZO T12 page displays SKU B08FT8VN57, $39.98, no reviews, over 6 hours per charge and 28 hours with the case, model T12, and a page battery field that says one lithium-metal battery. None of the four bodies supplies a controlled one-year retention curve, failure prevalence, independent same-condition comparison, battery-replacement route, complete warranty and return scope, or proof that a displayed rating predicts longevity.

nodes.subject: battery-health and chemistry boundary
nodes.object: The frozen state-of-health overview defines battery health relative to specification, says capacity and other useful parameters generally deteriorate over time and use, and says evaluation methods and application thresholds vary. The memory-effect overview defines true memory effect for nickel-cadmium rechargeable cells and says lithium-based cells are not normally subject to it, while also noting that rechargeable batteries have finite lives and lose capacity with age. These generic mechanisms make chemistry, age, use, temperature, cycles, capacity, impedance, and charge acceptance relevant, but they do not establish a universal one-year deadline, an exact retention percentage, or a ranking among FOYCOY, Plantronics, Soundcore, and TOZO. The four seller bodies also use different battery wording, including an anomalous lithium-metal field on the rechargeable TOZO listing, so a charging rule or chemistry claim must not be silently transferred across them.

nodes.subject: one-side symptom and service boundary
nodes.object: A single silent, low-volume, uncharged, or disconnected side is not by itself a battery diagnosis. The FOYCOY seller body says charging-contact oxidation can prevent charging or power-on and says an unpaired pair can leave only one earbud connected, with reset offered as a troubleshooting route. The generic pairing page defines pairing as the initial linkage that enables device communication, and the stereo page describes two independent audio channels, but neither identifies the cause of an exact earbud failure. The wired Sennheiser IE 600 thread reports left and right one-side failures and contains disagreement over cable versus driver causes even though the product is not true wireless. These sources establish multiple symptom categories and the need for diagnosis, not the prevalence or root cause of any captured TWS listing.

nodes.subject: community longevity scope
nodes.object: Preserve every community statement as a scoped report. The AirPods thread includes a heavy user reporting battery or sound annoyance around two years, a motorcycle user reporting repeated six-to-eight-month replacements under specific exposure and service conditions, a three-year user reporting reduced battery life but continued use, and an unsupported universal two-to-three-year claim. A different iPhone thread reports cheap wireless knock-offs with only about 2.5 hours per charge but daily use for over a year, separating per-charge runtime from service life. The Moondrop Sparks discussion says the case was not sold separately and contains conflicting claims about whether another case would charge or pair the buds. Models, workloads, sweat, pressure, accidents, support programmes, and jurisdictions differ, and none of these threads estimates population prevalence or ranks the four frozen listings.

nodes.subject: TWS longevity preflight
nodes.object: Before checkout, verify the exact seller and SKU, new or renewed condition, refurbisher and prior battery history where applicable, current price, return window, warranty issuer and duration, regional service eligibility, firmware-update path, reset and re-pair procedure, contact-cleaning guidance, and whether individual earbuds, charging case, or battery service can be obtained and paired to the exact model. Record a same-volume, same-codec, same-feature baseline for single-charge runtime, left and right discharge, charging reliability, reconnects, and dropouts, then repeat under the same conditions across the return period and later checkpoints. For a defensible longevity ranking, obtain exact-model multi-unit or longitudinal evidence that reports usage hours, charge conditions, environment, failure definitions, censoring, replacement handling, and sample size rather than converting seller hours, ratings, or cross-model anecdotes into a failure rate.

nodes.subject: longevity and support gate
nodes.object: A listing can enter the admissible purchase set only if its exact seller and condition, battery and case history, warranty and return, regional service, replacement earbud and case compatibility, firmware and reset path, and same-condition runtime and fault checks are acceptable to the buyer. The FOYCOY rating and troubleshooting body do not prove long-term reliability; the Plantronics and Soundcore routes add renewed-condition and prior-battery uncertainty; the TOZO route adds an inconsistent battery field and no displayed reviews. Because the frozen corpus contains no exact-model longitudinal durability comparison and leaves support routes unresolved, no unique current winner clears the gate. Keeping the current audio setup and deferring is required rather than selecting by rating or advertised case hours.
